record.question: When temperature of a conductor is approaching zero Kelvin. The mean free path of the free electrons in the conductor is proportional to
record.explanation: The printed page 3 confirms all four powers as supplied. Under the idealized low-temperature electron–phonon collision model, the single-particle scattering rate scales as T³ and the Fermi velocity is nearly constant, so the collision mean free path ℓ = v_F τ scales as 1/T³ (https://acangi.github.io/lecture_notes_solids_thermal/lecture_12.html, section 12.5.2). This is a conditional proposal: the stem does not specify the scattering mechanism or distinguish collision from transport mean free path, and residual impurity/boundary scattering can limit the path near zero kelvin.
